doc_verification.detail: Reachability: no doc_preflight.json sidecar exists in session/contract dirs; endpoint_registry carried a contract-build-time verification (source_status 'reachable', verified_at 2026-09-02T12:34:08Z); live re-check: WebFetch was network-restricted for api.qdrant.tech but the alternate web reader fetched the page in full (title 'Clear payload | Qdrant | API Reference', canonical URL matches) -> PASS. Version: page version selector 'v1.18.x' (URL segment v-1-18-x) vs target v1.18.0 -> major.minor match. Content: page prose 'Removes the entire payload for specified points.' grounds the constraint's payload-keys assertion; the page says NOTHING about vectors, so it supplies no vector-invariance grounding for the DEFECT oracle either (recorded, not a FAIL — the assertion itself is consistent). Endpoint: POST /collections/:collection_name/points/payload/clear == registry URL == script PATHS registration. All REST api-reference (no SDK confusion).

execution_evidence.log_pattern: DEFECT: (B) point 10 vector changed after clear — clear is payload-scoped — Type4_StateLogicViolation — backed by raw [B readback get_point] status=200 raw={"result":{"id":10,"payload":{},"vector":[0.9365858,0.09365858,0.18731716,0.28097573]},"status":"ok","time":0.000480632}; script uploaded VEC=[10.0,1.0,2.0,3.0] into a collection created with rt.setup_default(C,4,"Cosine"); the readback vector == VEC/sqrt(114) (exact unit-normalization: 10/10.6771=0.936586, 1/10.6771=0.093659, 2/10.6771=0.187317, 3/10.6771=0.280976); no readback was taken between upsert and clear#1, so 'changed AFTER clear' is inference from comparing stored-normalized vs raw-uploaded, not an observed transition
secondary_observations: [B/C/E readback] OK: payload exactly empty — the constraint's payload-keys assertion was SATISFIED at every readback; [D readback get_point] payload exactly {"c":2,"d":"y"} — no ghost-key resurrection; [C clear#2] repeat clear on already-empty target -> 200 completed (idempotent over own output); [B/E count] result.count=1 unchanged

[F non-existent point clear] MEASURED status=404 raw={"status":{"error":"Not found: No point with id 9999 found"},"time":0.004017179} — SKIPPED by-design per threat_model (rest: proper 4xx WITH a diagnostic naming the missing id)

comparative rest-face, same session, controlled probe output_boundary_collections_create_017.log:9 '[scroll bcc171cb4e3cos] status=200 raw={"result":{"points":[{"id":1,"vector":[0.6,0.8,0.0,0.0]}],"next_page_offset":null}' — norm-5 probe [3,4,0,0] upserted into a Cosine collection with NO clear anywhere already reads back unit-normalized; :12 '[scroll bcc171cb4e3euc]' [3.0,4.0,0.0,0.0] unchanged under Euclid control — normalization is scoped to Cosine and present at upsert time (017 verdict NO_DEFECT: 'documented by-design storage behavior confirmed')

comparative rest-face, same family output_state_payload_clear_003.log:14 '[raceB-r0 readback scroll] ... {"id":1,"payload":{"k":"v1","grp":"odd"},"vector":[0.47140455,0.23570228,0.47140455,0...' — point 1 whose payload was NOT cleared ALSO carries the unit-normalized vector [2,1,2,3]/sqrt(18): normalized storage is independent of clear

sibling reproduction output_state_payload_clear_001.log:17 'DEFECT: (F) point 1 vector changed after payload clear: [0.2581989, 0.2581989, 0.5163978, 0.77459663] != [1.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0]' — same pattern, readback == [1,1,2,3]/sqrt(15); scripts 003 and 004 report the identical 'vector changed' DEFECT — but all four scripts share the SAME setup (rt.setup_default(C,4,"Cosine")) and the SAME raw-vs-stored oracle, so the multi-script pattern is one shared oracle artifact, not four independent endpoint misbehaviors

http_semantics.note: no request-side-decidable error in the chain: all adjudicated probes are legal requests that returned 200; the only 4xx observed (F-probe clear on absent point 9999) is a genuine HTTP 404 with a diagnostic naming the missing id

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: after clear, targeted points carry no payload keys
contract_grounding.note: violates=False because the constraint was genuinely complied with: every readback (B/C/E payload exactly empty; D exactly the new dict with no resurrection; repeat clear 200) satisfies the payload-keys assertion. The DEFECT's trigger phenomenon (vector) lies OUTSIDE this quote's constraint domain, and a scan of all six constraint sections plus all 87 assertions found NO contract constraint covering vector invariance across payload operations — the 'vector intact' oracle exists only in the script's own docstring (candidates.jsonl constraint_id field arrived empty/truncated; constraint recovered from the script header 'constraint_ids: qdrant_state_payload_clear_001', which does exist in structured_contract.json state_constraints).

chain_links: contract: qdrant_state_payload_clear_001 exists in structured_contract.json state_constraints (assertion payload-scoped: 'after clear, targeted points carry no payload keys'); candidates.jsonl constraint_id field empty — recovered from script header

doc: https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/points/clear-payload reachable, v1.18.x, 'Removes the entire payload for specified points.' — grounds the payload assertion; contains no vector claim

script: raw requests mechanically correct (upsert VEC=[10,1,2,3] + payload {a,b} -> clear#1 -> clear#2 -> set_payload {c,d} -> clear#3 -> readbacks; all wait=true) BUT the adjudicating oracle vec_ok(stored, uploaded_VEC) encodes an uncontracted bit-exact roundtrip expectation under distance=Cosine, and no pre-clear readback was captured

log: DEFECT lines 20-21 ('point 10 vector changed after clear — clear is payload-scoped — Type4') are the faithful output of that oracle; raw responses show fully compliant payload behavior and a vector equal to VEC/sqrt(114)
chain_trace.break_detail: the script tested a phenomenon outside the contract's assertion domain (vector bit-exactness vs payload keys — milvus_030 wrong-phenomenon pattern) AND its causal reading is refuted by in-chain evidence: the controlled same-session probe boundary_collections_create_017 shows upsert-time cosine normalization with no clear involved (Euclid control unchanged), and state_payload_clear_003 shows normalized vectors on points whose payload was never cleared; source forensics confirm normalization runs in SegmentEntry::upsert_point while clear_payload never touches vector storage

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: claim path: REST POST /collections/{c}/points/payload/clear -> lib/shard/src/update.rs process_payload_operation:131 -> clear_payload:819 -> SegmentEntry::clear_payload (segment/entry.rs:808) -> payload_index.clear_payload ONLY — vector storage is never touched by clear. explanation path (where the vector value actually comes from): REST PUT upsert -> SegmentEntry::upsert_point (entry.rs:653) -> NamedVectors::preprocess (named_vectors.rs:296) -> preprocess_dense_vector:335 -> Distance::preprocess_vector (types.rs:329, Cosine arm at :337) -> CosineMetric::preprocess -> cosine_preprocess (spaces/simple.rs:228) unit-normalizes the uploaded vector BEFORE storage; GET point with_vector=true returns the stored (already normalized) vector ('vectors should be already processed', appendable_dense_vector_storage.rs:163). Callers do not re-validate or undo the normalization — it is the storage format for Cosine collections.

excluded: env (all requests 200, deterministic, reproduced by a controlled in-session probe)
concurrency (single-threaded clear/set loop; the 003 race variant shows the same normalized vectors on untouched points)

by_design: cosine normalization at upsert — source comment 'Equivalent to DotProductMetric with normalization of the vectors in preprocessing' (spaces/simple.rs:168) + storage comment 'vectors should be already processed' (appendable_dense_vector_storage.rs:163); confirmed behaviorally by boundary_collections_create_017 (norm-5 probe reads back normalized under Cosine with no clear, Euclid control unchanged) and by clear_payload's source path touching only payload_index
